title: London police officer testifies she forgot Mario Hamel was there
article: A London police officer testified Tuesday she failed three times to check on a prisoner who killed himself because she forgot he was there.
"I wish I was more diligent," Const. Brianne Sinclair told an inquest into the Nov. 25, 2010 death of Mario Hamel, 55.
"This is tragic and I am here because I don't want this to ever happen again."
Sinclair was a police cadet when Hamel was brought into police cells after being arrested for being drunk in public.
One of her jobs was to check on each prisoner every 20 minutes.
But three times after Hamel stopped moving in his cell, the first time only three minutes after, Sinclair checked nearby cells but not his.
Hamel strangled himself with his own shirt just before 3 a.m.
He ceased moving at 3:03 a.m. but was not noticed until another cadet did a physical check of the cell at 4:07 a.m., the inquest heard.
London police have since changed the cell check system, requiring cadets to use an electronic wand to touch buttons placed near cells.
That is supposed to ensure they walk to and look into each cell, the inquest heard.
